answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated work or collusive claims. A hollow profile gains no influence merely by multiplying accounts: each one must tie up capital, and a gale of disposable identities multiplies the attacker’s locked funds and exposure. The atlas of accepted work can record audit outcomes, so reputation accrues to identities that repeatedly deliver verifiable results, not to whoever creates the most names.
